text: Galileo Galilei observed four moons orbiting Jupiter in 1610, among them Europa and Ganymede. Centuries later, NASA launched the Hubble Space Telescope, which has photographed the Andromeda Galaxy and the Crab Nebula. Edwin Hubble had shown at the Mount Wilson Observatory that galaxies move away from the Milky Way. The European Space Agency operates the Gaia mission to map a billion stars. In 2015, the New Horizons probe flew past Pluto, a dwarf planet in the Kuiper belt, while the James Webb Space Telescope now observes exoplanets around TRAPPIST-1.

Marie Curie was a Polish and naturalised French physicist and chemist who conducted pioneering research on radioactivity. Born in Warsaw, she studied at the University of Paris, where she met her husband Pierre Curie. In 1903 she shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel. She later founded the Curie Institute in Paris, and during World War I she developed mobile X-ray units for the French Army. Her daughter Irène Joliot-Curie won the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1935.
